biography.plain_text: Thomas A. Moorehead is an American businessman who built Sterling Motorcars into a luxury car dealership group in Virginia. He became the first African American Rolls-Royce dealer and later sold the group to Lithia Motors. His business interests also extended into hotels and property, alongside educational philanthropy with his wife, Joyce.

long_biography.plain_text:
Automotive entrepreneur Thomas Moorehead left an academic career to learn car retailing under dealer James Bradley, a fraternity brother who became his mentor. His parents, both teachers, had hoped he would complete his doctorate. Instead, he mortgaged his home and used his savings to enter dealer training, following an apprenticeship that prepared him to run his first business.

Education remained central to his giving. With his wife, Joyce, he established a foundation that provided scholarships and emergency grants to students, as well as assistance to working families. Their support also reached historically Black universities. Later, the couple endowed a scholarship through the Girl Friends Fund for students pursuing business-related studies.
